title: Booking a dog into boarding kennels
context: You will hear a man phoning a boarding kennels to book a stay for his dog while he is away.

lines.t: Good morning, Hillside Boarding Kennels, Jenny speaking.
Hi, Jenny. I'm going overseas for a family wedding next month, and I need somewhere for my dog to stay. A friend of mine recommended you.
Lovely. I'll take a few details first. What's your name?
Mark Thibodeau. It's a French name, so the spelling is a bit unusual. T-H-I-B-O-D-E-A-U.
T-H-I-B-O-D-E-A-U. And your postcode, Mark?
8 0 1 4. Sorry, no, I always mix up the last two. It's 8 0 4 1.
8 0 4 1. That's Riccarton, isn't it? And what's your dog called?
We call her Juno, but her full name on the vet records is Juniper, so you'd better put Juniper, in case you need to call the vet.
Juniper. And what breed is she?
She's a cross. Everyone thinks she's part collie because of her markings, but the rescue centre told us she's actually a Labrador cross.
And how old is she?
She's six. Oh, no, wait, she had a birthday last month, so she's seven now.
And what dates do you need?
I fly out on the 12th of April, and I was coming back on the 19th. But the airline changed my return flight yesterday, so I won't be back until the 21st. So from the 12th to the 21st, please.

That's fine, we have space. Now, we've got three types of accommodation. There's a standard kennel, which is an indoor pen. Then there's a kennel with its own garden run, so the dog can go in and out whenever it likes. And there's our luxury suite, which has a sofa and a webcam, so you can watch your dog from your phone.

The webcam sounds fun, but I'll be too busy at the wedding to look at it, and I imagine it's pretty expensive. Juniper's used to having a backyard, so I think she'd be miserable shut inside a standard kennel all day. I'll take the one with the garden run.
Good choice. That's forty-five dollars a night. The standard kennel would have been thirty-eight. Does she need any medication?
Yes, she has tablets for her joints, one every morning.
That's no problem, but we do charge seven dollars a day for giving medication. So that makes it fifty-two dollars a night altogether.
Okay, that's fine. What should I bring when I drop her off? Should I bring her own food?

No need. We feed all the dogs a high-quality dry food, and it's included in the price. Some owners like to bring the dog's bed, but please don't, because they nearly always get chewed. The one thing we must see is her vaccination certificate. We can't accept any dog without it, I'm afraid.
Right, I'll make sure I've got that. And will I be able to find out how she's doing while I'm away?

Of course. We used to send owners a daily email, but a lot of people said they never saw them, and phone calls were tricky with people in different time zones. So now we send a photo by text every evening, just a picture of your dog and a quick note.
That's perfect. Thanks very much, Jenny.
You're welcome. We'll see you and Juniper on the 12th.
